html:
Switzerland's permanent neutrality was recognised by the great powers in 1815, at the Congress of Vienna and the Treaty of Paris that November.

The cantons had tried to stay out of Europe's wars since the defeat at Marignano in 1515, while still selling mercenaries. French invasion in 1798 and the Helvetic Republic showed what being dragged in cost. In 1815 the powers wanted a buffer between France and Austria and guaranteed Swiss neutrality and borders.

Switzerland stayed out of both world wars, though in the second it traded with Germany and turned away many Jewish refugees. Neutrality made it a home for diplomacy, from the Red Cross to the League of Nations. The Swiss joined the United Nations only in 2002.
sum: Switzerland's permanent neutrality was recognised by the great powers in 1815, at the Congress of Vienna and the Treaty of Paris that November.
